newsitem.title: USA: Simpson's lawyer argues police planted evidence.
newsitem.headline: Simpson's lawyer argues police planted evidence.

text.p: O.J. Simpson's lawyer told the civil trial jury on Monday that his closing arguments would take longer than expected since he must disprove the plaintiffs' contention there was no evidence of police planting evidence.
"I didn't anticipate Mr (Daniel) Petrocelli would stand up and say to you that there was no evidence of planting, no evidence of contamination, no evidence of tampering," attorney Robert Baker said.
"Just because he says it, doesn't make it so. There is evidence all over the place and we will prove it to you," he said.

Petrocelli, one of the plaintiffs' lawyers, made an emotional appeal in his closing argument last week for the jury to find Simpson responsible for the murders of his ex-wife Nicole Brown Simpson and a friend Ronald Goldman.
The ex-football star was acquitted by a criminal court in 1995 of the murders, but is facing a civil suit brought by the victims' families.

Baker, who apologised for a horse voice caused by the flu, said of Petrocelli's argument: "When he says there is absolute proof to a moral certainty that O.J. Simpson committed these murders, it is his rhetoric that is hollow."

He said the plaintiffs had skipped over any question of police planting evidence or investigators contaminating evidence. "We go straight from the bodies being found (June 13, 1994) ... directly to the lab tests," said Baker. "And that's all the information you need to know?"
The defence team, which has argued that Simpson was framed by a combination of police corruption and investigators' ineptitude, was to continue its closing arguments on Monday.
"I want to talk about what happened that night ... and how the police went about justifying their conduct that night," Baker said.
After a brief rebuttal by Petrocelli, Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki could give the jury instructions later in the day or on Tuesday and the panel could begin deliberations.
If found responsible for the murders, Simpson could be forced to pay millions of dollars in damages.
